name: draft-assistant-design-spec
sourceOfTruth: Draft_Assistant_reference.dc.html (pinned reference prototype in this bundle)
purpose: Machine-readable design spec for diffing a running build against a pinned reference.

drift.note: Token hex values supersede any earlier session brief. Earlier palette listed bg #0a0d12 / acc #7dd3a0 / positions b39ddb-4dd0b1-f2a65a-6fa8ff-94a0b0; the current build is in design-tokens.json.

files.describes: type roles, both theme palettes, radius, density, team colours
constants and step-by-step algorithms for availability, scarcity, verdict line, recompute, persistence
endpoints, payload shapes, nullability, field names
shell and overlay geometry, grid column widths, screen inventory, panel order
assertable checks, null-state matrix, the four principles
the same content in prose, for humans
one short spec per screen, for porting one screen at a time
backend integration history and open questions

knownGaps.detail: mock grid and opponent cards assume snake order; linear, 3rd-round reversal and auction are unimplemented
needs ~880px, gets ~708px at a 924px window; VBD and TIER fall off
field, slot and hotlink exist; no sample player has a real ESPN id
replace with the real bootstrapped width
client-side per pick today; anything heavier needs an endpoint and a latency budget under a pick clock
components are shown individually; four or more signals needs a design decision
server-side per league (pools validation across devices) or local until opt-in
if mock rooms can be read directly, manual entry becomes the fallback

prototypeDataCaveat: Availability figures, mock logs, calibration buckets, weekly finishes and three-season tables are sample or deterministically generated data, labelled on screen. 70 of 378 players loaded. Layouts, formulas and null states are final; the wiring is the work.
